places.name: Alum Rock Park
places.summary: Spacious park featuring hiking & biking trails, mineral springs & several picnic areas.
places.quote:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Alum Rock Park is a hidden gem in San Jose and the perfect escape into nature without leaving the city. One of California's oldest municipal parks, it offers beautiful tree-lined trails, peaceful streams, scenic canyon views, and plenty of shaded picnic spots. Alum Rock Park is known for its rich history, diverse hiking trails, and natural beauty.

We thoroughly enjoyed our visit, especially the tranquil atmosphere and the chance to connect with nature. The well-maintained trails are suitable for families as well as avid hikers, and there are several spots to simply sit back and enjoy the surroundings. If you're looking for a peaceful getaway, a morning hike, or a family picnic, Alum Rock Park is an excellent choice. It's a place you'll want to visit again and again.

places.name: Butcher Dog Park
places.summary: Spacious park providing areas for off-leash dogs, with separate runs for large & small pooches.
places.quote: Butcher Dog Park is a fantastic place for dogs and their owners to enjoy the outdoors. The park is clean, spacious, and well maintained, with plenty of room for dogs to run, play, and socialize safely. The separate areas for different-sized dogs are a great feature, helping everyone feel comfortable and secure. There are shaded seating areas, waste stations, and water available, making visits convenient and enjoyable. The friendly community of dog owners creates a welcoming atmosphere, and it’s always a pleasure to see so many happy, energetic dogs having fun. Whether you’re a local or just visiting, Butcher Dog Park is an excellent destination for exercise, fresh air, and quality time with your furry friend. Highly recommended—definitely deserves five stars!

places.name: Cahalan Park
places.summary: Popular, nearly 10-acre park featuring basketball & tennis courts, softball fields & playgrounds.
places.quote:
Cahalan Park is a fantastic community park that has something for everyone. The park is spacious, clean, and very well maintained, creating a welcoming environment for families, walkers, and anyone looking to enjoy the outdoors. The large grassy areas are perfect for relaxing, playing games, or having a picnic on a sunny day.

The playground is well designed and provides a fun, safe place for children to play, while the walking paths and open spaces make it easy to enjoy a peaceful stroll or get some light exercise. The mature trees offer plenty of shade, making the park comfortable even on warmer days.

One of the best things about Cahalan Park is its peaceful and friendly atmosphere. Whether you’re visiting for a quick walk, spending time with family, or simply enjoying some fresh air, it’s a wonderful place to unwind. This park is a great asset to the community and is always a pleasure to visit. Highly recommended，five stars!

There is a large field behind the elementary school, it is not fenced off, do not use the field during school hours.

There is a sand-based playground, and a separate grass area on the opposite side of the school field, separated by the sidewalk that cuts through the middle of the park. There are picking tables alongside the walkway as well.

There is a sign prohibiting dogs off leash, but the pathway is a popular place to walk dogs, and after school hours, the park is a community gathering area that locals bring their dogs to run off leash.

There is a separate playground on the far side of the school field, it can be used after school hours by the community.

places.name: Cathedral Oaks Park
places.summary: Park · good for kids.
places.quote:
A small park, mostly a single hill with some trees at the top.  If you're looking for a network of trails and long hikes, you'll want to go a little further afield, but a review of a hilltop hike should be about the views... and there are some nice views overlooking the neighborhood, city and hills in the distance.  (See photos.)

Good reasons to come:
* you want a quick walk, even a quick burst of cardio charging up and/or down the hill
* you want to enjoy a viewpoint overlook
* you want to chase the view at sunset (or sunrise, if that be your thing)
* possibly also to look for wildflowers and butterflies and the like in the spring (note: photos I've uploaded are from mid-June).

Do note that the hill is grassy, and depending on the season of the year and where local maintenance is at, you may prefer long pants and/or caution when bringing little ones or four-legged friends along.  (Check it out first.)

places.summary: Library · free parking and step-free entrance.
places.quote:
A humongous library in the heart of San Jose. I think there were like, 8 floors? Which is even more than the San Francisco Main Library! There is endless study space and an infinite catalogue of books. It really feels like a center for everything, as you can also find programs,  events, collections, and showcases here. I really liked their California collection! I think the library doubles as the college library for San Jose State, too, so there are some student resources and spaces.

The building is really beautiful, and the view gets better the higher you go.

The main reason I docked a star from the MLK Library is because I think it could be better maintained. Some floors were great, but other floors were awkwardly furnished and had missing chairs, broken outlets, empty bookshelves, and even spills and messes.

Other than that, it’s a near-perfect library. Overall, 4/5.

places.name: Lake Cunningham Park
places.summary: Park with sports fields · good for kids, free parking, and step-free entrance.
places.quote:
Lake Cunningham Regional Park is one of the best parks I’ve visited in the San Jose area. The park is incredibly spacious, clean, and well maintained, making it a great destination for families, couples, fitness enthusiasts, and anyone looking to spend time outdoors. The walking and biking trails are wide, scenic, and perfect for a relaxing stroll or an energetic workout while enjoying beautiful views of the lake.

One of my favorite features is how much there is to do. The playgrounds are fantastic for children, and there are plenty of open grassy areas for picnics, sports, or simply relaxing in the sunshine. The lake creates a peaceful atmosphere, and it’s a wonderful place to watch birds, take photos, or unwind after a busy day. There are also plenty of benches and shaded spots throughout the park, making it comfortable even during warmer weather.

The park feels safe and welcoming, with ample parking and clean restroom facilities. Whether you’re visiting for a morning walk, an afternoon with family, or just to enjoy nature, there’s something here for everyone. I was impressed by how well everything is maintained and how enjoyable the overall experience was.

If you’re in San Jose or the surrounding area, I highly recommend spending a few hours at Lake Cunningham Regional Park. It’s a beautiful place to exercise, relax, and appreciate the outdoors. I’ll definitely be coming back and would happily recommend it to friends and family looking for a peaceful and enjoyable park experience.

places.name: Selma Olinder Park
places.summary: 13-acre city park featuring athletic fields, picnic sites, BBQs & separate small & large dog parks.
places.quote:
If you're looking for a great park to visit with your family, Selma Olinder Park is definitely worth checking out. This beautiful park has a lot to offer, including a spacious playground area that is perfect for children.

Aside from the playground, Selma Olinder Park is a great place to take a walk or enjoy a picnic. The park  features plenty of green space, as well as benches and tables for visitors to use. There are also several paths that wind through the park, providing a great opportunity for exercise and exploring.

However, it's worth noting that there is an ever-present homeless danger along the Coyote Creek Trail, which runs adjacent to the park. While the park itself is safe and well-monitored, visitors should take caution and be aware of their surroundings if using the trail.

places.name: Seven Trees Community Center & Library
places.summary: Community Center with a gym, an auditorium, and event space · restrooms and step-free entrance.
places.quote:
Seven Trees Community centre is Best and well facilitated Community centre.
I've never been to a community center before, but I discovered that this one has a library, exercise room, gym, and several multi use rooms. In addition to that there is a county sponsored senior nutrition program that has free lunch for seniors (or they can donate $3 to support the volunteer run program).
If you come with a senior it is only $8 for non-seniors.
The warm colors and angles of this building are really interesting, and it is LEEDS certified to be energy efficient. There is ample parking and an outdoor play area for kids.
A great community resource for kids, adults and seniors.
